newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil Prices seen sliding on more supply.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil Prices seen sliding on more supply.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to drop some more this week due to prospects of more supplies next month, Manila vegetable oil traders said.
"Expect prices to remain below the $600 level," said a senior Manila trader.
Coconut oil prices hit a year-low last week when it pierced below the $600 per tonne CIF level due to the arrival of fresh supplies in Rotterdam, traders said.
Coconut oil supplies in Rotterdam surged to 14,424 tonnes as of July 21 from a mere 285 tonnes a week ago.
Prices fell by an average of $35 per tonne in the first three days last week and later gained $10.
"This week, expect prices to fall at least $10 per tonne as the Philippines approaches its historical peak harvest season for coconuts in August," said one trader.

Philippine coconut oil exports between July 1 and 23 reached 72,500 tonnes, up 21.5 percent from 59,671 tonnes shipped in the whole month of July last year, trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines Inc said in a preliminary report.
It said Philippine coconut products in the first seven months of the year reached 862,619 tonnes in copra terms against an actual 855,046 in the same period last year.
Traders said they expected the Philippines to export a total of 90,000 tonnes of coconut oil this month.
